title: Marriage Legislation Amendment Bill 2015
portfolio: (s) ENTSCH, Warren, MPGAMBARO, Teresa, MPBUTLER, Terri, MPFERGUSON, Laurie, MPBANDT, Adam, MPMCGOWAN, Cathy, MPWILKIE, Andrew, MP

speeches.speaker: Matt Thistlethwaite
speeches.brief: The speaker praised the marriage bill but focused on Australian aid to Papua New Guinea, citing a $33 million TB clinic that reduced drug-resistant TB mortality from 25% to 5%, and criticised the Abbott government's $11.3 billion aid cut for threatening similar programs.

speeches.speaker: Terri Butler
speeches.brief: The speaker seconded the Marriage Legislation Amendment Bill 2015, arguing that marriage equality should be legislated by parliament rather than delayed by a plebiscite, and citing human rights principles and the historical evolution of marriage.

speeches.speaker: Teresa Gambaro
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Marriage Legislation Amendment Bill, which removes discrimination by allowing any two people to marry regardless of sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or intersex status, while protecting religious freedoms and not permitting discrimination in goods and services. They thanked cross-party cosponsors, including the member for Leichhardt, Warren Entsch, and their chief of staff, John Lamont, for drafting the bill.

speeches.speaker: Cathy McGowan
speeches.brief: The member for Indi co-sponsored the Marriage Legislation Amendment Bill 2015, arguing for marriage equality and citing local Anglican Bishop John Parkes AM as the first senior Anglican cleric to publicly deem same-sex marriage inevitable. The speaker urged Parliament to legislate for justice, equality and fairness for all, including constituents Fleetwood and Ivy, while leaving religious institutions free to decide their own practices.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Nikolic
speeches.brief: The member for Bass argued that the definition of marriage should be decided by a national plebiscite after the next election, citing a local poll showing less than half of Northern Tasmanian voters support same-sex marriage and the need to respect both traditional and reformist views.

speeches.speaker: Adam Bandt
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Marriage Legislation Amendment Bill 2015 to remove discrimination from marriage laws, praised Warren Entsch and co-sponsors for their work, and called on Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull to allow a parliamentary vote instead of a plebiscite, arguing Australia lagged behind other developed English-speaking countries on marriage equality.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Wilkie
speeches.brief: Marriage equality is inevitable and should be passed now, with 72% public support according to Crosby Textor; Australia is the only developed English-speaking country without it.

speeches.speaker: Gai Brodtmann
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Marriage Legislation Amendment Bill 2015, arguing for marriage equality on grounds of justice and equality before the law, and opposed a plebiscite, noting that two-thirds of Australians support same-sex marriage. They also stated that a Shorten Labor government would introduce a marriage equality bill within its first 100 days and that no church should be forced to marry same-sex couples.

speeches.speaker: Tanya Plibersek
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that Australia should join the more than 20 countries that have legislated for marriage equality, criticising the government's proposed $160 million plebiscite as a waste of money and noting that government members including Cory Bernardi, Bridget McKenzie and Eric Abetz have said they will not be bound by its result.
